sections.heading: Davra Grivin Dilipbhai vs State Of Punjab on 6 August, 2024
Bench: Manjari Nehru Kaul
content: This order shall dispose of the above-mentioned petitions filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for grant of bail to the petitioners, as they arise out of same FIR i.e. FIR No.25 dated 07.08.2023 under Sections 420 , 383 , 384 , 466 , 468 , 470 , 471 , 506 , 120-B , 201 of the IPC and Sections 66C and 66D of the I.T. Act, 2000, registered at Police Station Cyber Crime, Phase 4, Mohali.
2. Mr. Praagbir Singh Dhindsa, Advocate, has entered appearance on behalf of the complainant and filed his power of attorney, which is taken on record.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners at the outset submits that though the investigation in the present case is complete and even charges framed, however, subsequent to the registration of the FIR in question the parties have amicably resolved their disputes, as a result of which the parties would be approaching this Court under Section 528 of the BNSS for quashing of the FIR in question on the basis of compromise.

4. In addition, it has been submitted that the petitioners have no criminal antecedents and have been in custody since 14.08.2023 and 02.09.2023 and hence, in the aforementioned facts and circumstances, further incarceration of the petitioners would serve no useful purpose.

5. Per contra, learned State counsel, on instructions from Inspector Gaganpreet Singh, has opposed the prayer and submissions made by the counsel opposite in view of the following allegations levelled in the FIR:-

6. Learned counsel for the complainant has not disputed the submissions made by the counsel opposite qua the parties having resolved their disputes. Learned counsel for the complainant also does not oppose the prayer made for granting the concession of bail to the petitioners.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the relevant material on record.

8. In the facts and circumstances as enumerated hereinabove, the instant petitions are allowed. The petitioners be admitted to bail to the satisfaction of the trial Court/Duty Magistrate concerned. However, it is made clear that anything observed hereinabove shall not be construed to be an expression of opinion on the merits of the case.
